strongest_angle: Researchers at the University of Queensland have successfully demonstrated the first proof-of-concept for gravity-based communication, transmitting binary data through physical barriers using a moving elevator counterweight.

key_facts.fact: Physicists at the University of Queensland used a 1.8-tonne elevator counterweight in the Parnell Building to transmit a binary message through a brick wall.
The research team successfully transmitted the word 'gravity' in binary code at a rate of one bit per minute, requiring nearly one hour to complete the transmission.
The experiment utilized a sensitive gravimeter to detect changes in the gravitational field caused by the movement of the elevator counterweight between two levels.
The study published in Science Advances by Andrew J. Groszek and colleagues explores gravity as an unblockable alternative to electromagnetic communication technologies.

numbers.label: Number of levels the elevator traveled between

quotes.text: All modern wireless communication technologies are based on electromagnetism. However, electromagnetic signals are readily susceptible to screening and blocking, so their availability cannot be guaranteed in adverse environments.
quotes.speaker: Andrew J. Groszek, Charles W. Woffinden, Michael D. Harvey, Andrew G. White, Matthew J. Davis
